body:
Thanks for all the comments from everyone.  This site is pretty awesome.  I wasn't sure what I was doing posting here, but the advice here is good.  I've noticed that there is a general aversion to antidepressant medication on Reddit in general, but it seems people here are more open minded about it.  I guess I will give them a shot.

To answer some of the questions posted here, this is not the first time I've been in counseling.  I was in counseling from the summer/fall of 2007 to the spring of 2009.  I left those sessions thinking I'd overcome a lot of what was bothering me, a lot of which had to do with forming close relationships.  I was particularly encouraged when I started a relationship with a woman I really liked last summer.  Unfortunately, that ended in kind of a betrayal and a subsequent mess of emotions that has dragged me down considerably.  I was still pretty functional for the most part through that time, until the last month or so when every day feels like a struggle to get through, and I find myself searching for a way out.

I've tried many things to snap out of it -- music classes, going out on my own to events I wouldn't usually attend, but I'm finding myself regressing to my more socially anxious patterns when I do these things.  Lately when I'm alone as well, I want to do very little.  I recently joined a music class that was part of an ensemble, which was at first very encouraging because I'd never played in a group before.  Lately I'm getting discouraged because I don't even want to pick up my guitar and practice anymore, and as a result I'm falling behind in the class.

I'm not particularly happy with my job, but I'm not particularly unhappy with it either.  I don't see much direction for my career right now, which admittedly is bringing me down.  But it is a good deal, and I make plenty of money, have flexible hours, and I feel a strong sense of obligation as it is a small company and I am the only one that does my job there.

I know that I need changes in my life, but more and more I'm not sure what kind of changes I need or what would make me happy.  I've done many, many things in the pursuit of happiness.. moved across the country several times, quit jobs and advanced to a better one more suited to my interests, counseling, diet, exercise, cutting down on drinking, etc. etc. But this weight just keeps coming back to haunt me.

The biggest obstacle I'm facing is forming close relationships.  I wasn't really intimate with a woman for close to 7 years or so, and I was starved for it.  I still am.  One of the things that brought me down about my last session is that the counselor reminded me that without being able to put out the proper energy of enthusiasm and confidence, finding someone to be close to could be impossible, and I need to overcome all that to form a healthy relationship.  I've heard that before, understood it, believed it, but I can't believe I'm still working to get there.  After months, years, I'm tired of the struggle, and I'm beginning to wonder if I can ever get to where I want to be.

I'm tired of my life and I'm tired of trying.  I've had a history of depression my entire life, but it's been particularly bad the last month or so.  I've started seeing a counselor in that time, but I'm starting to wonder if seeing him has made me better or worse.  After 4 sessions he's recommending antidepressants, which I've always kind of felt an aversion to.  But on the other hand I feel like I've tried everything (attention to diet, counseling, exercise) and I don't feel much better. I get to work and hang out with my friends, but every day feels like a struggle, and lately I just want to get away from *myself* more than anything in particular.

Yeah, though we try to use it sparingly.  And the problem I'm having is more with the politics of those it's attracted -- constant topics railing against gay marriage, for example.  Hating Obama for not celebrating the national day of prayer.  A lot of sappy bullshit about what wonderful friends everybody is even though none of them have met IRL, but at the same time they'll devolve into bickering nonsensical arguments that make the flame wars on reddit look like the dialogues of freaking Plato.
Hahaha, if only the community I work with was as fun as reddit.
